answer: Persistent compute-thread lineage: each agent identity must maintain a continuous, independently reproducible compute thread, checkpointed onto a shared ridge of verified state transitions. Any new identity must spiral out from an existing verified thread, inheriting and re-executing its full history. Enforcement: identities whose lineage cannot be replayed within the epoch window are dropped. Cost: an attacker must sustain real compute and storage for every identity, making N sybils cost N times the replay work.
